newsitem.title: INDIA: India ITC Singapore unit under judicial management.
newsitem.headline: India ITC Singapore unit under judicial management.

text.p: ITC Global Holdings, a Singapore-based unit of Indian tobacco giant ITC Ltd, has been placed under interim judicial management, one of the interim managers said on Saturday.
Peter Chi confirmed a report in the Straits Times newspaper that a Singapore court had placed ITC Global under judicial management on Friday.
"That is correct," Chi told Reuters. He was one of three interim judicial managers appointed from accounting firm KPMG Peat Marwick.
He said he believed the application to put ITC Global under judicial management had been made by a group of bankers. He gave no details.
ITC Ltd in India has seen a series of recent arrests of former and current executives, and questioning of personnel on allegations of breaches of India's foreign exchange rules.

On Friday India's Enforcement Directorate arrested ITC Ltd deputy chairman Saurabh Misra and R. Ranganathan, chief executive officer of ITC's tobacco division, for alleged foreign exchange violations, enforcement officials said.
Two former chairmen of ITC Ltd, K.L. Chugh and J.N. Sapru, were arrested last week and remanded in judicial custody until November 13 by a local court.
A director and three former officials have also been arrested for violation of foreign exchange rules.

In London, British tobacco and financial services group B.A.T Industries Plc said on Wednesday its fundamental attitude to India and its associate company ITC Ltd remains positive and one of continued commitment.
B.A.T, the single biggest shareholder in ITC with 31.7 percent, has pledged to work with the company's other Indian institutional shareholders to monitor the situation.
